>
> **What it shows on main: Quod replayed none of the 195 test steps, on all
> three repositories, and made no wrong replay.** Three gaps, each one a
> fix branch, explain every one of the would-be replays it executed instead:
>
> 1. **expr-lang/expr (Go)**: `ok  \tpkg\t0.001s [no tests to run]` is not a
>    line Quod's result normalization recognizes (it erases the duration only
>    when it is the whole third field), so each audit of a would-be replay
>    diverges on that duration and quarantines the key (4 of 20 history jobs,
>    22 of 45 traffic jobs, every re-run).
> 2. **tj/commander.js (Node)**: `node --test` prints `ℹ duration_ms 1541.8`,
>    not normalized either, so every audit diverges (5 and 29), the same gap
>    bench-lite shows on its fixture (docs/bench/lite-baseline.md).
> 3. **python-attrs/attrs (Python)**: the dependency step (`uv sync --frozen`)
>    installs the project itself in editable mode with a version from git
>    (`attrs-26.1.1.dev65`), and its `.dist-info/RECORD` differs on every
>    install, even of the same commit, so the test step's inputs never match
>    a recording (first difference under `.quod/venv/.../site-packages` on
>    every miss, re-runs included).
>
> The other misses are real changes (source, tests, `node_modules` after a
> dependency bump). commander.js's two oldest commits fail `node --test`
> plainly and through Quod alike (the project moved to Node's runner within the
> window), as does one PR head; they are counted, as the rule says.

# Quod on three small real repositories (bench-real-small)

## Summary

- **expr-lang/expr** (go, `go test ./...`, 20 commits): one CI job per commit took 47.5 s in total without Quod (median 3.0 s) and 60.2 s with it (1.27x). Quod replayed the test step on 0 of 20 commits. In pull-request traffic (each commit as its PR head, then its merge, plus re-runs) it replayed 0 of 45 test steps.
- **tj/commander.js** (node, `node --test`, 20 commits): one CI job per commit took 47.1 s in total without Quod (median 2.3 s) and 64.9 s with it (1.38x). Quod replayed the test step on 0 of 20 commits. In pull-request traffic (each commit as its PR head, then its merge, plus re-runs) it replayed 0 of 45 test steps.
- **python-attrs/attrs** (python, `python -m pytest`, 20 commits): one CI job per commit took 101 s in total without Quod (median 5.0 s) and 110 s with it (1.08x). Quod replayed the test step on 0 of 20 commits. In pull-request traffic (each commit as its PR head, then its merge, plus re-runs) it replayed 0 of 45 test steps.
- **Correctness: 0 wrong replays.** Every Quod result, replayed or executed, was compared with a plain run of the same source tree (exit code and output, durations aside; 195 results re-compared from the logs when this report was made).

## Method

For each repository, the 20 consecutive first-parent commits of its default branch ending at the pinned commit, all of them, oldest first (`git log --first-parent --reverse -n N PIN`). Nothing was picked or skipped. Three series ran interleaved on one machine (their order alternates per commit):

- **plain**: what a CI job does without Quod. A fresh checkout at a constant path (`git clone --shared`, new file times, as actions/checkout gives), the dependency install, then the test command, with warm caches that persist across commits (Go's build cache and module cache, npm's cache, uv's cache): a perfect `actions/cache`, the strongest baseline without Quod.
- **history**: the same jobs through Quod. The dependency install runs with network and is never memoized (`quod run --allow-net`); the test command runs `quod run --mode replay` (Go: `--warm`) with Quod's shipped trust settings (a result replays after one recording; the next two would-be replays of a step are re-executed and compared, then 5%). Audits Quod defers run right after each job (`quod audit`), timed separately and not counted in the job.
- **traffic**: realistic CI traffic, in its own Quod state: each commit first as its pull request head (a merge commit's second parent; the commit itself otherwise), then as the merge on `main`, then with probability 10% (seeded, 42) a re-run of the merge job.

Before the timed passes every commit's dependency install ran once plainly and once through Quod, so no timed run waited on the network. A job's time is checkout, install and tests.

| repository | license | pinned commit | dependency step | test step |

| [expr-lang/expr](https://github.com/expr-lang/expr) | MIT | `4b31df3a2e0e` | `go mod download` | `go test ./...` |
| [tj/commander.js](https://github.com/tj/commander.js) | MIT | `ba6d13ddb424` | `npm ci` | `node --test` |
| [python-attrs/attrs](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs) | MIT | `9d9f94a043de` | `uv sync --frozen` | `python -m pytest` |

Quod at main `3ddaaca`'s code (exp/bench-lite changes no crate; quod 0.0.0); go version go1.27.3 linux/arm64; node v24.22.2; Python 3.12.16; uv 0.13.6 (aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu); git version 2.39.5.

Hardware: CPU model not reported, 4 CPUs used (of 18), 7.7 GiB, aarch64, kernel 7.0.14-linuxkit, host `6f0cbbd5f685`.

## Raw data

Every step run is one line of `real-small-rows.jsonl.gz` (beside this file): series, phase, commit, tree, the exact command, wall time, exit code, Quod's outcome and phase times, the first input that differed on a miss, and the hash of the normalized output compared with plain. Logs of every run are kept beside it in the run directory.
